description: Step 1 - RSFC profile + cohort-avg + Schaefer init prior + spatial radius mask. Variant-invariant, mode-invariant.
source_note: `source` fields name the file owning the field's authoritative default. Line numbers are intentionally omitted — they drift on every reformat and the file/symbol name is the stable contract.
range_policy: advisory by default — `min`/`max` fields are UI hints documenting the values authors have validated; the parser/validator enforces only positivity (numeric fields) and enum membership (enum fields). Out-of-range-but-positive values are accepted at parse time. ENTRY-LEVEL EXCEPTION: `step1.threshold` IS hard-enforced to [0, 1] at parse time — a top-fraction outside that range is not a tuning question (FC binarization expects a fraction), so its `min` / `max` are part of the contract, not UI advice. See the per-entry `notes` field for the exception flag.
exclusion_criterion: Internal kernel-precision dtypes are intentionally NOT exposed in step1 even though they have function-signature defaults. Specifically: `run_generate_profiles.profile_dtype_reduce` (pinned at np.float32) and `run_radius_mask.dtype` (pinned at np.float32). These follow the validated CBIG fp32 convention; promoting them to user-tunable would invite silent 2x disk-footprint regressions with no quality upside. The runners' positional defaults remain authoritative for them.

entries.description: Top-fraction threshold for FC profile binarization.
entries.notes: Range [0, 1] is HARD-ENFORCED at parse time (`_validate_step1`); see the section-level `range_policy` exception clause. A value outside this range is meaningless for top-fraction binarization.
Only '0' is implemented; other values raise NotImplementedError at generate_profiles/profiles.py.
